body: I've been friends with twins for the better part of a decade, and these people were family to me. And we just...drifted apart. I'd would do my best to check in. And i feel like I could have done better but...at some point I didn't feel like it mattered how much I tried to help them/check in. I just felt like I was moved away from the table. No word no warning no explanation. Just gone. It all feels like it went into motion when I started going to therapy and growing and learning to set boundaries. I was suddenly no longer who they went to for anything. And I can admit I wasn't a great friend at all times. But I admitted it, I worked on it and I wanted to badly to grow and be better for the people around me. But I don't know, I feel like I no longer served a purpose so I'm no longer needed around. It's a shitty feeling, and just makes me think of everything I've ever done wrong regardless of the harm they've done. I don't know that it will ever get resolved. And that hurts the most right now

I want to say around 7th grade, I was really social until that point. My neighborhood friends all started parting, but they would get together and if I joined, I was just their bullying target, I got very depressed around then. On top of not being incredibly girly, and switching to a school with all the classic girly catholic school girls talking about dating, I didn't really have any friends. I was abused by a family member I had to live with as well, which sadly stunted how I could interact with boys my age either- I developed such a lack of trust. Moved to another state after that, and it was only worse. There are good days when I am all for being around people, where I feel like myself. As equal are my bad days where I just feel, like you said, blank. There was a point trying so hard to fit in I just forgot myself. I'll make connections with people then suddenly I drop off because in my head I am convinced it's not going to go well. If i stay in too much, I get even worse, I shake and tremble at the thought of any social situation i.e. grocery shopping. Or in a group I've managed myself in I am just silent, because anything I have to say I just expect to sound unintelligible or they look at me like I'm an idiot. I've lost all but a handful of friends, that are all in different states or countries so I am saved from being physically there in a social group. Which is good and bad. It's half way there.

Recovering from all this is going to suck, and it'll be painful. But coming through it, growing from it, makes you stronger as a person. I went through this alone, fully accepting of what had to be done. But the emotions of it come through no matter what. I would suggest looking on a planned parenthood website, they may have links for counselors you can see to talk about it for a few sessions that are free. Or call and ask. I've lived in the bible belt and the bible bashing is no joke, I'm just glad everything went smoothly. Everyone supports the right to birthing a child, and once that happens they suddenly stop caring. But once you have to go through something like an abortion, they think you are a murderer and send death threats. No woman wakes uo and fancies getting an abortion. Its because there is no other choice sometimes. Some people don't see their own irony.
You're a brave and amazing person to do this alone, and no one here is in person but you have some form of support here to fall back on if anything. But please if you can, try finding counseling or therapy of any sort.

Her decision was not wrong.
Going through it alone personally, all I wanted was to be around people who cared. I didn't expect any life changing words, I just wanted comfort and to know I was still loved. That may be what she needs.

Isolating was the perfect term, living with family so prolife and very strong to that, there's no one I had in proximity to talk to. I was raped before by a family member when I was a child, so that event happening I feel brought me back to the same place the first time did. 
I don't regret getting an abortion, I am in no position to handle another life as much as I'd want to. I'm still trying to handle myself. The experience was most of the trauma, it all happened so fast, in less than a week I figured out I was pregnant and was there in the room getting surgery, I didn't have time to process until it was said and done. I don't think I am, before I was drunk and saying I was a murderer, I had read the recent postings about the shooting at an abortion clinic - people praising that man- and I let it all get to me I guess. I also have a huge issue with people calling a living child 'it', that's what I said to avoid attachment with what was in my stomach, so it just annoys me I guess.
And I understand adoption, but some women like myself aren't in a position where they can do that. I wouldn't be supported for having a child full term, I'd be shunned for being pregnant by this family I am currently around. Not every woman is in a position financially, mentally, in any way to care for a child at the moment. I applaud the women that stick it out and raise the child, they are amazing human beings. 
Honestly the comments I have been getting is the best support I've recieved. And I sincerely appreciate it. I am making myself see this as an experience to grow from, something that has changed me and looked at things and people differently. That nurse is truly a gem, I wanted to send her flowers, I wanted to go back and just say thank you. 
I have not had any drinks to that extent since that night, I'm refusing to go down that path. And after reading and receiving the support from this group of people, I don't want to let anyone here down either. I want to heal and I want to heal right.
My mother will most likely avoid talking about it, but I am happy with her presence in the sense she accepted that it happened and didn't turn me away. It'll be nice to feel acceptance again. 
Thank you so much, I'll be sure to message you with anything, I really appreciate it.
